lesson_title: How India Elects Its Leaders: Prime Minister & President

scenes.purpose: Introduce the lesson topic and spark student interest.
scenes.teacher_script: Namaste, bright minds! Have you ever wondered how India chooses its two most important leaders – the Prime Minister and the President? Today, we'll explore their fascinating election journeys!

scenes.purpose: Explain the foundational concept of citizens voting for representatives, linking to general election qualifications from the textbook.
scenes.teacher_script: It all begins with your vote! Every eligible Indian citizen participates in elections to choose their representatives. Remember, to contest, a person must be an Indian citizen, at least 25 years old, and not hold any office of profit under the government.

attributes.text: Candidates can be from Political Parties or be Independents
Qualifications to Contest: Citizen of India, 25+ years old, no 'office of profit'

connections.to: Candidates can be from Political Parties or be Independents

connections.from: Qualifications to Contest: Citizen of India, 25+ years old, no 'office of profit'
connections.to: Candidates can be from Political Parties or be Independents

scenes.purpose: Introduce the election of the Prime Minister, explaining their role and connection to the Lok Sabha.
scenes.teacher_script: The Prime Minister is the head of our government, responsible for running the country. They aren't directly voted for as PM, but rather emerge from the Lok Sabha elections, where people vote for Members of Parliament, or MPs!

template_data.title: Electing the Prime Minister: Head of Government

attributes.text: Leads the Union Cabinet and advises the President
Elected indirectly via Lok Sabha elections

connections.to: Leads the Union Cabinet and advises the President

connections.from: Elected indirectly via Lok Sabha elections

scenes.purpose: Detail the step-by-step process of how the Prime Minister is selected after general elections.
scenes.teacher_script: Here's how it works: First, General Elections are held for the Lok Sabha, where voters choose their MPs. The political party that wins the most seats then chooses its leader. Finally, the President formally appoints this leader as the Prime Minister!

template_data.title: Steps to Electing the Prime Minister

stages.name: 1. General Elections (Lok Sabha)
stages.description: Citizens vote for Members of Parliament (MPs) across constituencies.

stages.name: 2. Majority Party Forms
stages.description: The party winning more than half the seats forms the government.

stages.name: 3. Leader Chosen
stages.description: The winning party's elected MPs choose their leader.

stages.name: 4. Appointed by President
stages.description: The President formally appoints the chosen leader as the Prime Minister.

scenes.purpose: Introduce the President of India, their role, and the concept of the Electoral College.
scenes.teacher_script: Next, let's learn about the President of India – our Head of State and the first citizen! Unlike the PM, the President is elected indirectly by a special group called the 'Electoral College'.

template_data.title: Electing the President: Head of State

attributes.text: Head of State & Commander-in-Chief of Armed Forces
First Citizen of India, upholds the Constitution

connections.from: Head of State & Commander-in-Chief of Armed Forces
connections.to: First Citizen of India, upholds the Constitution

scenes.purpose: Explain the composition of the Electoral College for the President, differentiating between MPs and MLAs.
scenes.teacher_script: The Electoral College for the President includes elected members from both our Parliament and the State Assemblies. This means elected MPs from Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, and elected MLAs from all states, cast their votes!

bullets: From Lok Sabha (House of the People)
Votes weighed by state population to ensure fairness

template_data.title: Who Forms the President's Electoral College?

scenes.purpose: Outline the simplified process of the President's election, mentioning proportional representation.
scenes.teacher_script: In the President's election, MPs and MLAs cast their votes. Each vote has a specific value based on population, ensuring proportional representation. The candidate who secures a clear majority of these weighted votes wins and becomes our President!

stages.name: 1. Electoral College Formed
stages.description: Comprises elected MPs and elected MLAs from states and union territories.

stages.name: 2. Voting Process
stages.description: Members cast their secret ballots using a proportional representation system.

stages.name: 3. Vote Value Calculated
stages.description: Each vote is assigned a specific value based on the population represented.

stages.name: 4. Majority Wins
stages.description: The candidate who secures more than 50% of the total valid weighted votes becomes President.

scenes.purpose: Assess student understanding with active recall questions.
scenes.teacher_script: Fantastic! We've covered a lot about how our top leaders are elected. Now, let's see what you remember with a quick quiz!

questions.question: Who do citizens directly vote for in a General Election for the Union Government?
questions.explanation: Citizens directly vote for MPs who represent their constituency in the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Which special body elects the President of India?
questions.explanation: The President is elected indirectly by an Electoral College consisting of elected MPs and MLAs.
